Phainon is a great many things. He was a model student (according to everyone but Prof. Anaxa), he is a fine roommate (though Mydei would disagree) and he'd like to believe he is an upstanding citizen (and ignores the fact that Aglaea still helps him do his taxes, even now).

What he, apparently, is not so great at, is being a streamer.

The night of the incident, Phainon had so hurriedly turned off stream that he had no time to bid his chat goodbye, or actually end his milestone broadcast. Who could blame him, though? When his roommate had stumbled into his room in nothing but a tanktop and sweats, he knew that he had to protect his chastity. Just Mydei showing his arm on stream was bad enough, because it would be downright unfair if Mydei were to show off more of himself just in that one clip.

Phainon is very aware of how the internet works. He knows that at least a quarter of his fanbase is there for his looks and he's not ashamed to admit that he does play into the fanservice, but it's an entirely different thing when someone like Mydei were to be subjected to such a thing.

Mydei was probably the type to still get his news by newspaper. The man had no social media that he knows of, and he just does a confused grunt and head tilt whenever Phainon or Castorice reference anything that isn't history, literature or combat related. What unholy things has the internet cooked up at the expense of his sweet, innocent, grandpa of a roommate? Just thinking about it made him shiver. Because while Phainon might be dull at times, he is, at least, more than familiar with Mydei's intrinsic...charms.

From the deep cut shirts he preferred to either the compressed t-shirts or sleeveless tanks Mydei wore, it increasingly felt like he had no decent clothing in his wardrobe. 'But even then,' he thought, 'a well dressed Mydei would surely send half the internet into cardiac arrest.'

He remembers the first time he saw Mydei dressed up. It was for some red carpet event Aglaea was invited to which she had, of course, declined to go. She had however sent Phainon and Mydei simply to use up the invites. And of all the things Mydei could or does agree to, Phainon will never understand why he had agreed to this.

Maybe it was to taunt him, or maybe this was some sick torture method he used because he knew that Phainon simply would not survive the image of Mydei, golden hair slicked back and muscle taut even under the layers of a sleek, black suit. 'By the gods,' he wondered, at the time, 'why does his suit have to be fitted?'

The gold and red buttons and patterning matched his red eyeliner, eyeliner that Aglaea had put on him. That dastardly woman.

Because Aglaea knew of the huge, embarrassing crush he had on the stupid, beautiful, disgustingly attractive man that was his roommate.

She must have orchestrated this as payback for something Phainon had done. He sighs, dragging a hand down his face. That night was beyond embarrassing.

Most of it, he spent tripping over himself at the mere sight of Mydei. He knows, at least, that some of it was justified, even without his own affection. Mydei was objectively beautiful, after all, and he's merely a mortal man, nursing attraction that he's kept hidden for over four years by now. He doesn't think he'd survive if he had to see that same thirst reflected in the internet.

He'll make sure to keep himself off Tweeter, just until this all blows over.

"Don't doze off," Mydei scolds, wacking him on the head with a spatula which he swiftly avoids, sticking his tongue out, "Go take a piss, wash your face. Do whatever. Just don't fall asleep yet. Your food's almost done."

After the stream, Mydei had dragged him to the dinner table and intimidated him into waiting by their counter until he finished reheating his dinner.

Phainon liked to believe that it was out of thoughtfulness that Mydei always made him his own portion, though part of him admits that it might just be because he's generally banned from kitchens. Still, he's grateful for the comforting view of Mydei's back towards him, humming softly as he tosses meat and veggies into his pan.

Mydei looks peaceful like this, he thinks as he yawns, stretching his back. The smell of Mydei's surprisingly delicious cooking wafting through their apartment.

In a moment, Mydei drops what must be a triple portion of beef stir-fry, noodles and steamed broccoli onto the table, unceremoniously shoving it towards him, not unlike one would treat a dog bowl. Phainon couldn't even complain, though. You never bite the hand that feeds you.

Well, not unless that hand was formed in a fist, pointed straight at him, as it so often was during their weekly boxing sessions. It was only then that he would not be opposed to biting.

Still, the food tasted heavenly. It was like he's never eaten before.

"By the gods, Mydei," Phainon says, "I think I just might be in love with you."

Mydei recoils in what must be disgust, and replies, "You're delirious. And disgusting. Swallow before you speak, have you not learned any manners?"

Phainon sighs, but swallows his food anyway. He's half asleep once food finally enters his system, and he almost passes out immediately on the dinner table. "My heartfelt praise met with insult to both my character and wellbeing. Truly, no one appreciates my talents."

"At least you know that much," he deadpans, "You're dead on your feet, though you've only been sitting playing video games. When did I start rooming with a child?"

"Well excuse you," he says, yawning, pointing a fork at him as a chunk of beef hangs on its end, "this child is also your only sparring partner at the gym. Pray tell, who else would box with a madman like you?"

Mydei sighs, "Sing praises of your physicality when you're not half dead, HKS. And eat your food, properly."

"Aha!" He exclaims, "So you're saying that I am your match at my best? Is that right?"

"What I'm saying is that you are far, far too self-satisfied," he shakes his head, in place of an answer, "you've been awake for nearly an entire day. Any more and you might truly keel over and die, and I do not wish to have to find another roommate." Mydei says as he flicks a dangerously strong finger towards his forehead. Phainon dodges with a grace that does not translate to his gameplay.

"Is this your way of saying I'm irreplaceable, Mydei?" Phainon goads, eyebrows inching even despite the exhaustion, "If so then I must admit, I'm quite flattered. To think you cared so much for me!"

Mydei mouth opens, instinctively to deny it, if only for the sake of being contradictory. But he pauses for a moment, then two, before sighing. "And if I say yes," he starts, "would you listen to me and rest, Phainon?"

Phainon stills immediately.

It's unfair, really, the power he has over him.

Mydei doesn't imply things, not in the way any others would. He does not ask, he makes demands. Not unlike a prince and not unlike a god reshaping the world to what he sees fit. That isn't how Phainon always views him, not all the time, but it certainly is a description he would often find apt.

Mydei doesn't admit things, either. Not that he does not apologize, or does not realize things, no (he is surprisingly sensitive to etiquette in that regard). It is just that he does not spell things out.

Most often, what he'll get is the faint twitch of an eyebrow and a sigh that means more than it might for others. Because Mydei expects him to keep up. To understand, somehow, the complexities of the walking enigma which is himself.

Yet sometimes, he does not make demands with the authority that seems almost natural to him. Sometimes, he speaks with a certain cadence. With a desperation, almost, that is so very vulnerable and human yet so much like him, that Phainon wonders how he'd ever mistake him as a god.

This, this is one of those times.

"I- Mydei-"

"You're running off fumes, Phainon," he says, with a subtle worry even Phainon rarely sees, "don't argue with me. Not on this."

And Phainon does not fight him, when he speaks this way. Because Mydei does not demand things he deems unimportant.

"Okay," he answers, settling back on his chair, "I'll rest, after this. I promise."

So he finishes his dinner and isn't immediately annoying for the sake of it, and washes the dishes afterwards.

He stumbles into his room and barely misses switching off the lights, groaning because he can't be bothered to get up again. He flops onto bed with an overwhelming tiredness he only now feels come all at once, and he passes out immediately, just like that.

(If he were awake, for just a moment longer, he would catch his door creaking open. He would notice the light switching off and gentle hands, unexpectedly so, covering his frame with a blanket.

And would notice the faint twitch of his lips, and would hear the whisper of 'hyena', fond as anything. A word now only meaningful to the both of them. He'd see fingers, twitching, itching to reach out and card through tangled yet soft white locks.

Alas, he is not awake. And so the man bids him good night in a foreign tongue and slips out, another promise tucked away in his chest.)

Chapter Notes

"You're streaming again?" Mydei asks, raising an eyebrow.

After years of living together Mydei has, inadvertently, memorized Phainon's streaming schedule. He often streams in the evenings, a habit picked up from his time at university, and does about four streams a week.

The man almost always streams while Mydei is out, streaming all throughout the weekends while usually only streaming once during the weekdays as well. Oftentimes, he finishes just around the time that Mydei comes home, so the two can have dinner together.

'It's convenient!' Phainon had reasoned, back when the two had only just moved in together. Mydei thinks it was just a ploy to have someone else cook for him, because Phainon was an absolute menace in the kitchen, but he agreed anyway.

They were broke college students who simply wanted to save money on groceries and dishes. The routine made sense, at the time. Mydei would cook and Phainon cleaned up after, and they'd split the bill for groceries, every month. It was efficient.

But four (nearing five) years later, they've long outgrown the necessity of the routine. However, Mydei finds himself unwilling to part with it. The habit's grown on him. Much more than he'd like to admit.

"It's a short stream this time!" Phainon smiles, "Last stream was- uh, irregular in a way. I just have some things to clear up today, that’s all!"

Mydei rolls his eyes. " Why you're streaming is none of my concern. I was only affirming that it will not go for as long as yesterday, will it?

Phainon chuckles awkwardly, he’s pretty sure he’s never doing a 24-hour stream again. “It’ll be a while until I reattempt such a stream. Why?” he goads, clearing his throat, “Worried about me?”

“Nonsense,” Mydei huffs, but he’s smiling anyway, “I’ll be off. Don’t order takeout- I’ve made lunch in the fridge. Just microwave it. I don’t want you near the stove.”

Phainon cringes at the memory. “Hey, that was one time!”

“And in the one time I took a trip out of town, you quite nearly burnt our complex down, boiling boxed mac and cheese. I will not hear any protest.” Mydei replies, glaring at him.

“Okay, okay,” Phainon raises his hands in surrender, “whatever you say, your majesty. Now go on, your clients are waiting for you.”

Mydei shakes his head and huffs what would’ve been a laugh on anyone else. “You have nerve to lecture me on punctuality, HKS,” but he grabs his keys and heads to the door anyway.

“You better not run away today,” he says, flashing a smirk before he goes. “I’ll be seeing you tonight, Phainon."

Phainon gapes.

He doesn’t even have a chance to respond before he’s off, the door clicking shut behind him.

Silence.

Only the faint steps of Mydei’s combat boots out the door echoes in the hall.

One step, two steps, and another, and another.

And then, truly silence.

Phainon crumples to the floor.

"Fuck," he says, to no one in particular.

His face is burning and he's so giddy he's going to trip up over himself. "He can't just say my name like that," he mutters into his arm.

Mydei is straightforward, impossibly so. Yet at the same time he never fails to say things that just don’t make sense. How could he say that? How could he say it so easily?

It’s like it’s intentional, almost, but in no way can he picture Mydei talking like that on purpose.

‘Does he know?’ he thinks, rubbing a hand over his face, ‘Is doing this to taunt me?’

Four years together and sometimes, he still doesn’t understand Mydei. The man is as straight-laced as he is an enigma. The way he commands respect yet never demands it of anyone. He’s the most ruthless and yet caring person he’s ever met. Fuck, he really is in love with him.

Dealing with the affection he's harbored for his roommate and best friend for years is a far more daunting task than he expected. It's gotten so bad that most interactions with him ends in either him blushing or making a fool of himself. More than usual, at least.

Because his feelings have never faded. Not since the day that they first met and not now, either. He's gotten no closer to neither confessing nor getting over him.

And he's not so foolish to expect anything to come out of this crush. What he wants is simply to maintain what they already have. This cozy, surprisingly domestic, life they’ve built together is beyond anything he could've imagined having with someone like Mydei. With someone who’s far, far too good to him already.

The only thing he's learned from his years of yearning is that rooming with Mydei will always be very, very bad for his heart.

He stays on the floor for a little while longer to collect himself. Breathing in, and out.

Today’s going to be a long day.

"Chat for the last time, I do not have a boyfriend!"

The stream had started off fine. It had started off good, even.

Most of it was discussing the stream, harmless questions he was supposed to answer to end off his milestone. Like: " why did you start streaming?" And " how are you so bad at games?" And "is your hair naturally that white or do you bleach it that often and that's why it looks so dry?" Normal questions.

It was then that someone in chat had mentioned the 'Mysterious Man' caught on stream last night. Like piranhas to blood, chat snagged onto it immediately.

Phainon huffed, "Come on, if I were dating anyone, which I'm not, I'm sure you all would have found their identity already. You all are terrifying."

There are a number of routines Phainon's created over the years. Ones he hold like tradition.

Habits define a person. Commitment defines a relationship.

For Phainon, it’s routine that defines trust. A lunchbox pre-made for him, the trash can wordlessly always emptied, the fridge always stocked with exactly what they need. Habit, routine, whatever it is; it’s because of the little things that you’re alive. They build your home and your day-to-day. They’re personal, almost sacred, in a way.

And so he likes to stick to his routines, in doing what is comfortable and what is needed in the way and cadence he has trained himself to do.

(And when you allow someone else into these routines, that itself is love.)

This, running down the stairs of his apartment, out of breath and in grey sweats and a hoodie and t-shirt he yoinked off a chair, this is also a routine.

Phainon streams once every weekday, but he rarely streams on Wednesday, and almost never on Wednesday evenings. Because every Wednesday, at six, Mydei finishes training his clients, and he works the closing shift that night. Every Wednesday, he spares a little over an hour to close up the gym, as Phainon makes his way there.

Because Wednesdays are when the gym is finally, truly empty, and they have the boxing ring all to themselves.

It's nothing too fancy, and Phainon himself doesn't often visit, but it was Mydei who initially suggested they box. It wasn’t too far-fetched of a suggestion. The both of them had taken different forms of martial-arts in college, just as an extracurricular.

Mydei, specifically, had joined sports clubs all throughout his high school years as well. So Phainon had actually considered getting back into the sport.

When asked, Mydei had reasoned that Phainon needed the exercise because his 'weak gamer body will keel over if you don’t start moving.’ Phainon had rejected, of course, because the thought of going to a gym with Mydei might actually send him into cardiac arrest, but the other was surprisingly insistent on him going.

He remembers the first time he stepped into the gym, around the first time Mydei took a PT job.

He didn’t have any expectations- hell, he didn’t even know what a personal trainer did. But nothing could’ve prepared him for the sheer magnitude of what he saw.

Because the thing is, most people can’t even handle Mydei normally .

Back in University he was so popular among both the men and women that he was voted as hottest faculty member despite barely even participating in any events. The library’s foot traffic increased by 61.57% (he’d know, because he wrote a research paper about it once for a project) since Mydei started working as assistant librarian.

Point is: Mydei is unequivocally hot .

Imagine then, the sight of him. Six foot four, sweaty, shirtless and leaning on the rails of a boxing ring, muscles taut and tattoos spanning over well-defined shoulders as he stretched. His golden hair shining under harsh, artificial light, making his red-tinted ends glow.

‘Shirtless,’ he thought, as he gaped, because he really couldn’t think of anything else, not in the moment. ‘Holy shit.’

At the time, it felt like half the gym was staring at him, too. While the man in question was uncaringly giving advice to his client in the ring, who was nodding far too enthusiastically to only be thinking about boxing .

Phainon scowled. It was indecent for his (crush) roommate and best friend to be so blatantly ogled like this! While it wasn’t uncommon for acquaintances- strangers even, to be rendered speechless by his mere presence, isn’t seeing him like this just a bit too much?

(If he weren’t fuming, he would’ve noticed the triumphant smirk Mydei had thrown him from across the room, and the subtle shake of his head as he dismissed his client).

That day, once the gym had been properly cleared out for the night, Phainon sat him down by the ring and tried very, very hard to speak seriously.

“Mydei,” he started.

The other raised a brow.

“I’m going to hold you hand while I say this-”

“Please do not.”

“But you need to wear a shirt. Please.”

The look in Phainon’s eyes was dead serious. Like the idea of Mydei being shirtless in a gym where over half the people were either shirtless or wearing minimal clothing was something to be worried about. The whole situation was so absurd that Mydei was at a loss on whether he wanted to laugh or cry.

He punches him instead.

“What the fu- I’m being serious!” Phainon whined, nursing his bruised cheek. The purple bloomed across his pale skin and Mydei immediately felt guilt bubble up in his throat.

“Shit- I thought you would’ve-” he sighed, running a hand through his hair, “it’s my fault. Reflex, sorry,” he mumbled as his eyebrows pinched.

“I’ll…find something to treat it. Stay.”

Phainon was about to tell him not to bother, but the other had already stood up to go find a first aid kit.

He watched as he looked around stumbling, almost, in a haste to find the supplies.

Mydei fretted silently, so unlike the rest of him. His care had always been through his actions. His worry in the form of hurried hands and quickened footsteps. He always tended to fret when it came to other people, and he always took it to heart, even if it didn’t show.

But Phainon didn’t want to be a source of worry. Not to Mydei.

“It’s not even that bad,” Phainon whispered once he returned. He said it quietly, as if saying it too loud would make it untrue, “it looks worse than it is, promise.”

Mydei scowled, unbelieving. “We haven’t even boxed yet you’re already injured. And it’s my fault.” He said again, holding out an ice pack as he gently rubbed salve on the bruise, his hands grazing the others cheek.

“...does it hurt?” he mutters, tentative, eyes fixed on the blossoming purple and blue.

From here, he could barely see Mydei’s expression, shadowed by his hair, backlit by the lights. All he could feel was the faint tremor of his fingers, calluses barely touching the warmth of his skin.

Phainon gulped, heart leaping into his throat. “No,” he answered truthfully. “Not at all.”

It was a weird night.

While it was supposed to be their first boxing session, Mydei had for some reason refused to even entertain the idea of stepping into the ring after the punching stunt. Instead, Phainon was just told to sit and wait as he finished closing out the gym.

They had takeout that night, a rare occasion where Mydei didn’t feel like cooking. He even let Phainon pick the restaurant and offered to pay as well. Thinking back, that might’ve been the start of their ‘loser pays for dinner’ tradition. One that Phainon has overwhelmingly been disadvantaged by.

Because in around the 2 years since they’ve started, he's only won three fights against Mydei thus far (current tally: 99 to 3).

So now Phainon goes to the gym once a week to get beaten up for half an hour. And it's fun, for the most part, and surprisingly good stress relief (and a good reason to spend time together).

That is, when he actually remembers to show up.

"Mydei!" Phainon huffs, a bit too eager, a bit too excited. "I’m sorry I’m late!" He says as he catches his breath, leaning on the gyms glass doors.

“Four minutes and twenty-eight seconds,” Mydei notes, not looking up from his phone. “You’re on time,” he smirks, "How commendable.”

Chuckling, Phainon takes the time to recollect himself. “You know me,” he says, breathless, “I don’t make promises I don’t keep. And I’ve got a good feeling tonight. It’s about time you treat me to dinner isn’t it?”

Mydei laughs now, amused and excited, his eyes glinting like a predators. “We’ll see about that. Come, don’t keep me waiting, Phainon."

Stepping into the ring, he cracks his knuckles, “100 wins, counting tonight. Quite the milestone, isn’t it?”

“You haven’t won yet, Mydei!” Phainon slips into the ring as he takes his hoodie off, settling into a familiar stance.

And it doesn’t take long before Mydei lunges .

Like with all things he does, Mydei fights with intensity . Every blow and every shift in his legs is intentional. Almost deadly. He fights, for lack of a better word, like a beast.

They trade blows and jabs and he feels his muscles strain from the exertion. He’s sweating and his fists are bruised, and it’s like the whole world has narrowed into this ring, into just the both of them. It’s electric.

Phainon side-steps a jab straight to his jaw, retaliating with a hook that Mydei brushes off with a grunt. “And when did you become a thief? Stealing my shirt without permission?”

He smirks, caught. He hadn’t even noticed. Throwing another punch, he taunts, “Distracted now, aren’t we?” Phainon ducks as he aims an uppercut, straight to the underside of Mydei’s jaw, which he blocks without even glancing.

“Hardly.”

The fight goes on like that, equally matched, neither of them giving an inch. It’s addicting, how they fall into a state where nothing else matters. Nothing but the next step, the next punch the other throws. It’s by this point that every muscle in his body is screaming for a break, and yet he can’t stop. Not when he’s confronted with Mydei, the lines of his body carved with unadulterated might.

It drives him insane, how different this side of him is. Untethered and fiery, like a lion stalking his prey. Phainon feels a shiver run up his spine, excitement thrumming in his bones.

This is a side of him he very rarely shows to anyone else. Not to his clients, not to other gym-goers, and barely even when he’s alone. Just him, Phainon thinks greedily, just for me.

Mydei steps forward, winding up for another punch which Phainon ducks, earlier than he has before, and sweeps his legs from underneath. Mydei falls with a grunt, his long legs causing Phainon to stumble as well.

He barely catches himself, inches away from the other’s face. But he's down, he thinks, I win.

“Hah-” he pants, high from the euphoria of it all, from winning. “Ninety-nine to four. It’s my win tonight.”

Mydei looks dazed, blinking blearily. His mouth hangs open in measured yet erratic breaths, his eyebrows lax and eyes so alive. Every breath makes Phainon all the more aware of how sheer the other’s black tank-top is. Slick with sweat, the droplets disappearing into the deep cut of his shirt, running down his collar and pecs. The red of his tattoos glow against the tan of his skin and all he can think is that red really is his colour.

It’s so unfair, he thinks, how good he looks like this. His cheeks red and exhausted, and his usually fiery mane now even more disheveled. His braid, the one Phainon himself often weaves in the morning, starts to come undone from the exertion.

He reaches out instinctively to run his fingers through the strands. Mesmerized, as gold mixes with red.

Mydei’s eyes flicker, satisfaction settling into the lines of his face. The hard of his muscles unwound not into submission, but simply an admission of defeat.

“Cocky,” he mutters, mouth curling into a slow smirk, “but a win is a win. Congratulations.”

He reaches a hand out, as if expecting Phainon to help him up, and it’s only then that he snaps out of his trance, realizing the position he’s in.

One of his legs is between Mydei’s thighs, his arms on either side of his face. He feels the heat radiate off his skin. They’re so close he can smell the honeyed soap Mydei always uses. The one Phainon recognizes by scent after buying it so often when it’s his turn to do the groceries.

The inside of his mouth goes very, very dry.

“Ahem-!” he looks away, suddenly embarrassed, “I- let’s go for dinner! Yeah!” He springs up, willing a smile on his face, “your treat?”

Mydei blinks, running his tongue over the white of his teeth.

“Yeah,” he breathes, “whatever you want.”

‘Whatever you want’ turns out to be dingy American fast food from a restaurant Mydei refuses to step into.

“Come on!” Phainon whines, “You said anything!”

Mydei’s nose wrinkles in disgust, “This hardly counts as food, idiot. Could you not have picked anywhere proper?”

For some reason, Mydei hates fast food. His obsession with health and fitness is commendable, truly, and Phainon respects him all the more for it but come on? How could anyone hate fast food?

“It’s cheap!” He reasons, “It opens till late and it’s convenient! Now come on, don’t be a sore loser.” Phainon drags the other’s hand into the relatively empty restaurant. Mydei’s feet are planted firmly by the door.

“You act as though you do not already have enough money to buy out this franchise,” Mydei groans, but he eventually gets dragged in anyway, body exhausted from a day’s work.

Phainon smiles, satisfied, “There’s nothing wrong being frugal, Mydei.”

And truly, he does believe in his words. His parents always reminding him to spend wisely even while living in the big city. But generally, he just likes the novelty of fast food. There weren’t any locations like this back in his hometown.

“You ought to be grateful for this kind of convenience, your majesty,” Phainon says, thanking the tired-looking waiter who brings their food over, “we certainly didn’t have this back in Aedes Elysiae.”

Mydei mutters something under his breath as he nods to the server as well. “Have you called them recently? It’s the start of the month, is it not?”

“Yeah,” Phainon nods as he digs into his burger, “I called mom yesterday. Dad told me to call again tomorrow though, Cyrene wasn’t home at the time.”

His parents own a ranch out in the countryside, their family having a longstanding history with textiles and garments and such. While Phainon wanted to move out into Okhema for university, his sister Cyrene had stayed to continue the business.

He hums, he really should visit soon.

Mydei huffs, “That’s good. Tell your parents I said hi.”

Phainon rolls his eyes, muttering 'I did that already. They ask about you more than me.'

They settle into silence afterwards. The restaurant’s fairly empty, only the cashier standing behind the counter to accompany them. The warm, yellowish light flickers above as if struggling to stay awake. It’s comfortable, he thinks, this is nice.

“Is that really all you’re eating?” Phainon asks, pointing to the single chicken wrap Mydei had ordered.

It's comically small in comparison to Mydei's relatively large hands. The bulk of him curls up just to pick it up properly.

He sighs, “I do not trust the ‘food’ here. I’ll eat a proper meal at home.”

Phainon tuts as he wags his finger. "We can’t have that. Come on," he gestures, "let’s order something. Why don’t we split some ice cream to go?”

Mydei pauses at that, contemplating.

Bullseye, he smiles.

Despite Mydei’s generally low tolerance for unhealthy habits, he does have a soft spot for sweets.

It used to surprise him, just how often the other baked to fulfill his sweet tooth. Back in college Mydei had fans just because of the baked goods, candies or chocolates he brought to the lectures he was in. Hell, even Professor Anaxa liked his food.

“That is…not too bad a suggestion,” he relents, “but we are not purchasing any here. There’s a gelato shop down the road I’ve been meaning to try. We’ll walk.”

“Your wish is my command,” he bows with exaggerated flourish. Mydei rolls his eyes.

“You’re making a fool of yourself. Eat, and stop the theatrics.” Phainon chuckles as he settles back into his seat, quickly finishing his meal.

The two walk out not long after.

It’s a bit too cold a night for ice-cream, and they’re both a bit too underdressed for a night walk, but if they were uncomfortable, neither of them comment on it. They’re standing side to side, shoulder to shoulder, and if Mydei huddles closer, he reasons it’s just for the warmth.

It’s nights like this that he’s grateful for his habits. It’s times like this that he’s glad for routine. Because it’s only in the night, once both their days are over, that truly, they may exist with each other.

The street lights are bright in the holy city, making visibility high even late at night.

Yet if anyone were to have spotted their hands brushing close, he’d argue it was a trick of the light.

"I want ten!" Trianne says. "I'm gonna eat so much I'll be sleepy! Then tomorrow can come faster!"

Mydei shakes, fond and soft and thoroughly amused. “We don't have enough for ten, but we can start with five. How ‘bout that?”

A chorus of cheers accompany the man as they make their way to the kitchen. Phainon settles by the counter with a sigh, thankful most his babysitting duties are over. In truth, he most greatly prefers nights like this. When it's the both of them babysitting or cooking or whatever it is they're doing together. It’s all achingly domestic.

It's in moments like this, in the quiet of their home and in the time between what they spend together, that he truly feels like he's walking on eggshells. A part of him he doesn't want to recognize as himself whispers that this is what he has to lose; what he will lose if he chooses to confess haphazardly. Not the fear of rejection, but of what will come with it.

A house of cards is what he's built. Grand and beautiful yet deceptively fragile.

Phainon's not an insecure man, not really, but he cannot help but feel incompetent when he's done nothing but receive help. He'd moved to Okhema to pursue a degree he barely cares about simply to escape a life he ended up dooming his sister to. Even after the move he's basically been handheld by Aglaea up until Mydei had entered his life and more or less acted as his caretaker.

He wants to confess, he knows he does, irregardless of what happens after. But can he? Should he?

Even if Mydei were to accept, would it truly be better if they'd gotten together?

(He doesn't know. Doesn't know if he wants to find out, anymore.)

His musing is broken by Trinnon tugging softly at his pant leg, blinking blearily as she gestures to be lifted up. Phainon gently settles her down in the chair next to him.

“It’s alright if you wanna nap, Trinnon,” he smiled, slightly tired, “the three of them are gonna be busy for a while.”

In lieu of a response, she merely places her little hand over his. “Snowy, you're thinking a lot.” She mumbles, “Like Agy. But not like Agy. You're thinking bad thoughts.”

Of the triplets, Phainon could confidently say that Tribbie was the most outgoing, but Trinnon was the most observant. She’s quiet: more so than Tribbie and definitely more than Trianne, but she was quiet by normal standards as well. Yet somehow, she makes up for it through sporadic bursts of wisdom. Words that somehow strike harder than any normal criticism, imbued with the innocence of a child and said frankly with a heart that truly cares.

Phainon sighs. “They’re not bad thoughts,” he mutters. “It’s just. Adult thoughts. I’m alright, Trinnon, don’t worry.” He doesn’t want to worry her, really. Enough people are already burdened by his love life.

“Hm,” she tilts her head. “but Snowy, I’m still worried.”

Fuck , he thinks, and doesn’t say, because he knows better than to swear in front of a child. Now he can really tell why kids often prefer Mydei over him.

Despite his (mainly useless) degree in psychology and the hundreds of thousands of words he’s churned out in University, his mouth grows dry when confronted with such honesty. What could he say to placate her, when he cannot make sense of his own thoughts?

“Sorry,” is what he settles for.

“It’s okay,” is what she replies.

She's silent for a second, before continuing again. "Tribbie's favourite colour is blue," she starts.

Phainon stays silent, waiting for her to continue.

"But Trianne likes red. And I like both," she says. "We share things, though. Plenty of things. Do you know what our room is?"

"Um," he pauses, "either blue or red?"

"Both," she says, instead. "Our room is purple."

Phainon doesn't really understand, but he nods anyway. Trinnon shakes her head, almost in disappointment, but she drifts asleep not long after right on the stool.

He sighs, frustrated- not at her, or at anybody else for that matter, but merely at himself. His emotions have gotten so obvious that the kid he’s babysitting noticed. Sweet as it was for her to comfort him about it, even he knows that he's being pathetic. He’s a grown man with a puppy crush and too much fear to act on it. His friends know about it. His sister even, a hundred miles away, knows how simply gone he is for his roommate. It’s gotten to a point that it’s so, so much harder to ignore than it once was.

It might’ve been a crush, or plain attraction, or even simply loneliness, at a point. But he’s gotten so used to living this life, has gotten greedy enough to want it for himself. Because he’s gotten a taste, and now he wants seconds, and doesn’t know how much more Mydei will give him.

(He knows, deep down, that there’s no backing out. He knows he doesn’t want to ignore it.)

Phainon feels like a fool. A lovesick, helpless, fool.

He groans into his hands and thinks of red and blue, and he wonders how the hell he'll reach purple.

He feels like he's going insane.

The tripod in her right hand looks like a scythe, the way it cuts through the air with sheer force, capturing the chase with shockingly steady hands. “His cookies are the one line not to be crossed. Whatever happens now is penance , Deliverer.”

Forget inconspicuous , he thinks, they haven’t even entered the convention and are already making a scene.

He truly wonders how Aglaea deals with the both of them. She might be a saint, or simply a very terrifying woman. He considers calling her just to get this madness to end.

“Casto, work with me here!” He chuckles nervously as Castorice continues hounding him, “It was a joke! I'm sorry, I swear! I’ll never wear them again! I won’t touch your cookies! I’ll throw those glasses out! No, I’ll wear them for the entire day! Ack - Just stop chasing me!”

Phainon yelps as he slips through a crowd, muttering apologies as he narrowly avoids con-goers. “Please ?” He adds on, because he’s polite like that.

Castorice, of course, ignores him. For some ungodly reason, she manages to keep up with him. Fueled by sheer disgust at his fashion choices and retribution for the glasses and cookies he’s stolen, she catches up to him while being weighed down by a tripod in her right hand.

Well , he thinks as Castorice tackles him to the ground, at least it’s good content.

Mydei was a sort of boogeyman figure for the streamers within Phainon’s circle.

They all know about his, quote, “stupid hot brute of a roommate”. Yet Phainon himself had denied romantic (or sexual) attraction to said roommate.

But Aglaea knows the truth. That he was neither stupid nor a brute nor merely a roommate . The description was wildly inaccurate, even by Phainon’s standards.

Personally, as the only person to actually know the two, she finds the whole thing ridiculous. Aglaea’s been working tirelessly for the better part of a year to get the two together, yet nothing seems to work. From the dates and the red carpets and that ridiculously expensive Luofu couple's trip. She’d planned each attempt extensively, fronted the costs herself and for what? No progress. Nothing at all.

Tribios has seen the extent of her romantic endeavors. As in, her endeavors in making the two see the romance that was so plainly in front of their eyes.

The other woman has accompanied her through coffee breaks turned therapy sessions, and late-night dress fittings fueled by caffeine and rants.

“There’s no way,” Aglaea muttered, her third cup of coffee of the night once Tribios’ gown once again had to be adjusted. “There’s no way they don’t know. They must be joking. They're secretly dating and are using me to plan their wedding. There cannot be any other explanation.” She said, manic.

Aglaea is proper. Elegant. Almost inhumanely so. But she is also wildly passionate about the strangest endeavors, Tribios thinks as she laughed.

Aglaea sighed as she simultaneously started trimming and weaving fabric once more. Her talent for multitasking truly was a marvel. Tribios chuckled once more as she comforted her, gently patting her shoulder.

“Now, now,” she tutted, “your friends’ romantic troubles aside, I think it’s better you get some rest, Agy. And some dinner. Their love life and the dress can wait.” She said, gently prying the scissors and thread away from her hands.

Aglaea simply sighed, long-suffering.

Back then, she vowed that the two will end up together before she finished the dress (or before Comic Con arrived).

That was weeks ago.

And evidently, they are not together yet.

She’s told herself then to simply to ignore the two. That she has much, much more important things to handle.

And yet, their romance (or the lack thereof) is simply a travesty she can’t look away from. It’s an insult to her very nature as a romantic everytime she sees them so painfully in love and so painfully unaware of it.

Cyrene, her partner in crime, had even started giving up on the two. Their situation is simply that hopeless.

Just the thought of it is stressful enough. Aglaea puts her head in her hands and tries very hard not to scream in public. Castorice rubs her back soothingly.

Phainon is, despite the annoyance, a family friend.

He is someone she’s regretfully come to care about even through the periodic heart attacks he causes. He is good to a fault, a purity that would be naive on others but just earnest enough to be sincere on him. And it is undeniable to everyone that he would be happy with his roommate, and that in fact he had only started being happy once he’d met him.

She remembers his first weeks in Okhema.

When his family had first reached out about her watching over their son she was…hesitant, to say the least. She was capable enough, sure. By then her career had already allowed her a comfortable living. Yet, she didn’t know where the boy would fit in her life.

It’d already felt so full. Everyday she had a new project to do or an old one to revisit. If Aglaea could be described in a word, it would be that she is dedicated. Devoted, even. To her passions yes, but also to her missions. Whether that be taking care of the triplets or styling the mannequins around her home in whatever outfits she fancied at the time.

She was content. Perfectly so.

And so she didn’t know what exactly came over her when she accepted.

It could’ve been attributed to Cyrene’s constant begging or perhaps Tribios’ gentle encouragement to know more people. It could’ve even been on a whim, maybe of the need for a male figure for her garments, she wasn’t quite sure.

But if there’s one thing Aglaea is sure about, it’s that Phainon was absolutely miserable the first time he arrived.

He was smiling when they first met, a hollow, surface thing she’d seen through immediately. One for appearances, for being polite. Yet it didn’t quite fit on his face, with the almost dejected eyes he had. It was like he was missing a home he’d only just left.

He was wide-eyed but unsure, almost hesitant of the city, like it would eat him whole.

Aglaea sighed. It was just like Cyrene had said. That Phainon had always felt just slightly out of place.

She didn't understand then why Cyrene thought sending him her way would do him any good.

“Phainon, was it?” She greeted.

“Ah- yes, Miss Aglaea.”

She didn’t usually mind the overt respect, Aglaea was a highly sought after woman after all. But the dejected puppy stare Phainon had coupled it with made her queasy.

“Just Aglaea,” she shook her head, “you must be hungry, your journey’s been long. Come.”

Aglaea had brought him to a fast food joint that day, not quite sure what men his age might like. Phainon’s slightly brighter smile when ordering on the touchscreens was well worth the few hundred credits she spent.

He ordered a relatively small meal despite Aglaea offering to pay. A burger and meal set that seemed more fit for a child. That couldn’t nearly be enough for a man of his height, especially after such a long trip.

And so she excused herself to buy two more sets, both to go, that she slides over to Phainon without a word.

“I- Aglaea it really is quite alright,” he muttered.

Hesistant to accept help. She raised a brow, “Well,” she answered, “I’ve already bought it, no? I’d rather not have any. Feel free to do what you wish with it.”

Phainon hadn’t replied, so Aglaea took it as her own personal victory and steamrolled on.

“Your parents have arranged that you stay in my apartment until the academic year starts,” She said.

Phainon nodded listlessly.

"So, have you decided what to major in?" She opted for casual conversation, refusing the fries Phainon offered. Pleasantries were much easier than showing concern, even if they were a bit awkward.

“Not really,” he chuckled, a little sad, “my parents told me to take agriculture. Or animal sciences. The useful degrees, y’know? For the farm, or something.”

“I asked if you have decided, Phainon. Not your parents.”

And Phainon simply blinked at that, before eating the rest of his meal, which was alright. Silence meant that he was thinking about it.

Aglaea knows the burden of choice well. Choosing what fabrics to use, which commissions to take and how her garments must be designed. They feel monumental despite its entirely subjective importance.

So she lets him think, even as they walk home and Phainon asks with the most hopeful eyes she’s ever seen on a man whether or not he could “feed the stray dogs a burger.”

She’d told him no, of course, fast food would probably actively be worse for whatever animal eats it. But his dejected expression was potent enough that she considered going back on her word.

That night, Phainon slept in the living room, despite the guest room Aglaea offered. He scrolled through majors and landed on whatever would let him meet the most people, and help him fill up his time.

When he finally decides on psychology, late in the first night he spends away from home on the couch of someone he’s never met before, he wonders, still, if the choice he made was right.

“Aglaea, I appreciate you, you’re great, but If there’s one thing I cannot compromise on, it’s that I cannot do panels!”

Aglaea rolls her eyes.

“You can’t do a lot of things, Phainon. But they’ll kick you out of the lounge if you don’t participate, and the staff have already called for arrangements.”

“Sorry, the staff has what?”

Phainon never fights against Aglaea.

In fact, he agrees to a lot of things. Half-dates with his roommate? Sure. Random home visits? Sure. Stealing his coffee machine for weeks at a time? No big deal. Even throwing out most of his clothes (which is why he steals Mydei’s so often) is something he’s learned to live with!

But never. Never has or will he do a panel live.

“Oh come on. What difference is a panel and a stream, anyway?” Aglaea challenges, once Phainon refuses for the upteempth time. “You answer questions in front of a live audience, just as you do on your streams. I don’t see why a panel would somehow be any worse.”

“It’s live , Algaea, that’s exactly why it’s worse!”

The thing about streams is that he picks the questions. Which also means he chooses what he wants to ignore. That includes spam questions, personal questions. The ones he generally avoids answering for his safety and privacy .

Because the reason why he started streaming in the first place was as an escape. As a way to blur the lines of where he ended and the Deliverer started.

The difference with panels, however, is that questions are shoved in his face. That he can’t do Professor Anaxa’s patented three-step diversion technique. And considering his fans and his own pattern of answering questions, he already knows what his panel is going to be full of.

“They’re gonna make me talk about Mydei, damnit!” He groans, falling to his knees. The embarrassment is going to eat him alive, he knows. On a panel with mics shoved in his face and reporters itching to know about his love life.

Aglaea raises a brow almost in confusion. “You’re most worried about addressing the mystery man? ” She questions.

“ Fuck - yes! I’m worried about addressing my mystery man,” he wails.

Phainon is ugly sobbing on the floor and Aglaea considers it a grace that she is only slightly disgusted. She has half a mind to step back, chastising him for being dramatic, before she pauses.

A panel. Where he’ll be forced to confront the topic of his mystery man. His roommate.

And suddenly, in a motion too faint to be noticed by anyone who isn’t watching, she smirks, a gently cunning upturn of the lips.

“I have a proposition.” She starts.

Aglaea kicks him, just gently with the tip of the heel, to get Phainon’s attention. His head lifts up red from where it was glued to the ceramic. Gross.

That way, the both of us can take over in the case that your questions go awry ,” she adds, “ and to top it off, you’ll be able to get your collab content. All at once. Convenient.”

It’s a good plan.

One that she herself is quite proud of.

The catalyst for failure, as she's observed, is that they both too easily deny their feelings for each other. Somehow, there is always a convenient emotional or physical mishap that stops them from confessing.

Yet this, this plan might finally be foolproof enough to handle it.

She smiles.

Maybe the two won’t be so hopeless after all.

“Phainon. If you lose to me you’re paying for my cab back home.”

“That’s not fair!” He groans.

They both know he’s going to lose.

His escape from the Phainon who is caught up and in love and impulsively ran away from his old life in Aedes Elysiae.

Mydei shouldn’t be here. Shouldn’t be where Deliverer is.

All his friends only know of his ‘mysterious roommate’. With the exception of Aglaea, they only know Mydei as the guy who bakes and insists that Phainon bring gifts for his friends. As the guy who’s shirts Phainon always wears and the reason why he shows up on stream limping (because of sparring) or bruised (because he got punched in the face).

But they don't know more than that. They shouldn’t know more than that.

He makes it a point to separate his real life from anything on the internet. Because it’s easy to confront his issues and talk about the Mystery Man when he’s behind a screen and streaming. But it’s an entirely different issue for Phainon to confront the feelings he has for his roommate.

Mydei being here doesn’t even make any sense, he rationalizes.

He hadn’t told Mydei his plans for the day, and Mydei himself has his own set of plans.

Either whoever he saw wasn’t Mydei (unlikely) or Mydei just happens to be here completely unrelated to him (even more unlikely).

Phainon groans.

He could hope for the best and very easily just go back to Castorice and mind his own business. Assume it was just a blip in his imagination, something caused by Mydeimos withdrawal, or something.

But then he remembers his panel.

The one with three of the biggest Okheman streamers around. The one where people are, inevitably, going to bring up the Mystery Man. The one maybe-Mydei might watch at and see exactly how inexplicably in love he is with his roommate. The one where people will no doubt reference the online documentation of him ogling at his roommate's arms.

Phainon’s legs catch up quicker than his mind, eyes dead set on finding him again.

The possibility of Mydei seeing any of that is downright terrifying.

Fuck, he thinks.

Panels really are the worst.

Chapter Notes

Mydei is a conspicuous man.

Be it his tattoos, his eyes, eyeliner, jewelry, his body, or a combination of his features, Mydei is someone distinct, especially to Phainon.

While others could recognize him by his chunky golden earrings (the ones he’d only wear when at events or gatherings), Phainon could recognize him by his ears alone. The jagged sort of puncture they’d done back in college on his lobe, the tremor of the needle in his hands, a tacit confidence in him to do something potentially dangerous to him.

“Get on with it, already,” Mydei growled from where he settled on Phainon’s lap.

“Oh, hush! The last time I checked, I’m studying psychology, not learning to become a body piercer.”

“Yeah? And I’m not a paying customer. Now hurry up, it stinks .”

Their cramped two-person dorm was made into a makeshift studio, the scent of disinfectant and their one-burner gas stove turned up high to quickly heat the needle. Phainon’s cinnamoroll desk lamp (a gift Mydei had gotten him on a whim) shone straight into his eyes from where it hung precariously off his shelf. They’d huddled their beds together because they didn’t have a couch and Phainon refused to do it on their floor.

“If it stinks for you, it stinks for me too! At least take me out for dinner after this!”

Mydei snorted, “And risk an ear infection by going out? I’d have thought you were against such dangerous prospects.”

Phainon groaned, placing the needle back off to the side. His hands were still shaking, he couldn’t risk it. “This whole thing is risking an ear infection. Remind me, why couldn’t you just go to your tattoo artist again?”

Mydei shrugged, “They’re closed for the week.”

Phainon’s eyes narrowed at the deadpan response. Most people think Phainon is the annoying one. That Mydei puts up with him with growling and barely contained anger, that everytime Phainon eggs him on, Mydei is just that much closer to snapping.

He’s heard the whispers of when they’re together on campus. Mydei’s popularity is a given but he isn’t so blind to think that he doesn’t have his fair share of admirers as well. However they only like him in passing, in his smiles and the way he greets classmates and remembers people's names. He knows they find him insufferable, sometimes.

And so the moments when Mydei doesn’t act that way– when he’s all snark and sarcasm, instead of growling and pissed off as people say he should be, when he plays with the punches thrown at him instead of just shutting him down, Phainon finds himself at a loss on what to say.

“And you couldn’t just wait a week to get your ears pierced? You’d rather risk your underqualified best friend to do it?” Phainon sighs, shaking his head.

Mydei’s head is still on his lap, the rest of his body relaxed on the conjoined beds. He cracks his eye open and raises an unfairly defined brow. “Self-consciousness is a bad look on you, HKS. Where's your usual bravado?”

“Confidence is for things I can either do or bullshit my way out of. Possibly amputating your ears is not the time to be blatantly confident, Mydei.”

“My ears will be fine. I can handle it.” Mydei’s body does not move, but the infliction of his tone already indicates a shrug.

Mydei settles back, somehow relaxing even further to lay against his thighs. Phainon’s wearing sweatpants, the thick material of it one of the few good pieces of loungewear that he owns and Mydei seems to agree, the way he’s nuzzling into the fabric. Mydei often did that on soft fabrics and such. It was cute, not that he’d admit it.

They’re sitting in what feels like a nest of their combined blankets and pillows. It’s soft, comfortably warm, a satisfying sort of silence that makes even the smell of disinfectant almost cozy.

Phainon resists the urge to card through his natural hair and undo the braid that’s starting to come undone. Yes, natural, because Mydei’s hair isn’t dyed (he’s checked– none of his hair has ever discolored or faded), an earth-shattering realization he’s been forced to come to terms with ever since they’d become roommates. The strands naturally fade into blonde and gold up from where his scalp is, darkening into auburn red. It’s miraculous.

A marvel of nature, really. All of him is.

“Quiet tonight, aren’t you?

Phainon realized, then, that he’d unconsciously been leaning down with how closely he’s staring. Mydei’s eyes are blessedly still closed. He clears his throat. “I’m simply pondering how anyone’s let you study for a medical major. Home-piercing goes against every health and safety rule I know of.”

“And you would know all about health, wouldn’t you, philosopher?” He huffed, and from here he can see his faintly pointed canines, the slight crookedness of his smile. His breath smelled like the on-sale litre of mouthwash they share, and the remnants of diet soda, the only fizzy drink Mydei lets him consume.

Phainon feels an overwhelming urge to kiss him.

It was not the first time he’s felt so.

“Rude,” Phainon says instead.

Mydei is all hard edges and stoned stares, the sharp flick of his eyeliner unforgiving in the same way his gold necklaces hang heavy on his neck. He smells of rubbing alcohol and smoke from the stove, but so close like this he can smell expensive pomegranate soap– one of the few things Mydei always splurges on, and scent of cinnamon leftover from the snickerdoodles he brought to class this morning. He smells like the shitty college dorm that he gladly calls home.

Mydei is all hard edges, and Phainon is glad he has thick skin.

Phainon lightly pokes his cheek, marvelling at how the barest hint of baby fat still clings to his cheeks even despite the sharp jawline, before lightly dragging his finger down the length of his tattoos. He trails lower until his hand slips under Mydei’s loose shirt, eliciting a gasp as he tickles him in the he knows will get the other to laugh, so hard that he falls off the bed.

Mydei laughs all the way down and up, even after he stops tickling. “Stubborn,” he huffs, breathless as he grins, hair disheveled from the floor.

Mydei settles back on their beds, and Phainon walks over to the kitchenette to reattempt the piercing. Yet, after a few more attempts of Phainon heating and reheating the needle, the metal starts to blacken and there Phainon decides to take a break.

“If you can’t bring yourself to do it, just admit that you can’t. But you are taking me for dinner after wasting my time.” Mydei says. He’s sat down now after getting bored of lying and waiting for the needle that would not come.

“I’m wasting your time? Are you not the one who dragged me into this on a Friday night? A million things, Mydei. A million things I could be doing instead. I could have been out— partying, or something. Networking. Yes, that’s the word.”

Mydei stared at him blankly, leaning to sit up against the wall. “We both know you’d be spending your weekends with me either way. It was either this or the library.”

It wasn’t untrue, but Phainon is nothing but a contrarian.

“You never know that! I could be switching things up occasionally! I’m a young, healthy college student, I can do whatever I please. I could go to a bar right now, and prove you wrong.”

“Switching things up means going to Okhema’s museum instead of the sports center. You doing something different means us getting ground turkey instead of chicken.” Mydei emphasizes with a roll of his eyes.

“Oh shut it,” Phainon shuffles closer just to elbows his side, settling in the space next to him, “I have a youthful spirit! You just make us sound like we’re boring.”

Mydei pushes his elbow away, huffing an amused half-laugh. “Are you not? How ironic when grocery runs and Nietzsche are where you find most enjoyment. You yourself seem to be quite the ‘ boring’ person.”

“Oh? Speaking of philosophy now, aren’t we? Who’s overstepping into whose field of study, now?”

“Still you.” Mydei elbows him back, eliciting a groan. “Do not make it my issue that I happen to be better read.”

Phainon rubs at his still sore side as he glares. “And here I would have never thought that you’d be an existentialist.”

“Calling me a brute again? It seems you’ve run out of insults.”

“Well perhaps my boring day to day has dried off my capability of creative comebacks. You should be celebrating. Aren’t you always complaining that I’m annoying? That I’m a scoundrel?”

“A Hyena,” Mydei clarifies, because that’s what he focuses on, “I call you a hyena, and a scoundrel, because it’s true.” He pushes up against him, closer, so close their thighs stick to each other and he can feel every flex of his muscle even through his shorts.

Phainon huffs, looking away.

“Then why stick around? If I’m so annoying and you’re so tired of me,why trust me to pierce your ears or spot you at the gym? It’s not like you to be so undecided about things.” He feels himself exhale sharply through his nose. He doesn’t mean to be confrontational, nor unpleasant.

This is hardly anything to be offended about– a strange nickname, of all things, is tame in comparison to quite literally anything else people have done to him, Okheman or Elysian alike. But it’s Mydei calling him such things, and he finds it difficult to be so unaffected.

Phainon startles suddenly as Mydei presses his cheek against his shoulder. The softness of his cheek digs into Phainon’s bare shoulder after opting to wear a tank top for the night. Like this, the slight height difference between the two is noticeable, Mydei just barely shorter than him, able to rest his head without spraining his neck. Phainon goes very, very still.

“Mydei-”

“Shush, for once in your life, can't you listen? ”

Mydei’s voice drops, huskier than his usual baritone. Commanding in the way it wishes to be heard, oppressive in that it takes up his whole body to do so.

“Look at me. Look. Do I seem like I’m tired of you, Phainon?”

Phainon’s backs away like he’s been burned, then around, then facing him again, only to stare. The harsh light of his lamp only further frames his silhouette, half lit in shadow. It brings out the gold of his eyes, the gold of his hair, the gold of his necklace.

And oh , he realizes, Mydei would look really good in earrings.

Two earrings, gold and chunky, with a gemstone embedded inside. He doesn’t even need to think about what colour the gem should be. It was only natural that it’d be blue.

Mydei’s mouth pulls back into a slow smirk to reveal the white of his teeth, the slight glint of his canines. “What’s spooked you now, HKS?”

You. He thinks to himself.

The thought of him, the memories of him, the future he wishes to have. He wants more of this, of Friday nights doing unimaginably small, new things together. He wants the grocery runs and arguments on how spending more on turkey for less meat is worth it. He wants to get him earrings, wants to watch him wear them, wants to trail his tattoos further down than just on his arm.

He wants to be roommates after they graduate. He wants this shitty college dorm to be an apartment, wants to travel and visit old libraries so Mydei can see the original texts of the books he loves.

A sharp intake of breath, shaky, then immediately, he starts wheezing.

“Ohfuckohshitohkephaleourburnerisstillon-” He says in one breath.

Mydei’s head snaps as he roughly stands from the bed, rushing to their kitchenette. “ Shit that’s why it smelled so bad! Damnit, HKS!”

Phainon laughs as he coughs, hacking the smell of disinfectant and gas, quickly rushing to vent open his windows. “ Damn ,” he laughs, slumping over the window, “my bad, my bad! I didn’t realize it.” The strong smell of rubbing alcohol must’ve masked the scent of gas. He really hadn’t noticed it until then.

He hangs off from the outside of their dorm on the first floor, and when Mydei comes back with a cold water bottle in his hands, pressing it straight against his cheek, Phainon thinks that might’ve been when he first fell in love.

Maybe it was the fumes, or the delirium, but he’d worked up the courage to finally pierce Mydei’s ears afterwards to be met with the most deadpan “that wasn’t so bad now, was it?”

And when the earrings he’d commissioned (with over two years of savings, plus whatever money he got once he started streaming) finally arrive, Mydei wears them and immediately decides they’re far too heavy, yet he keeps them and uses them as often as he can, anyway.

Phainon could recognize him anywhere. From more than the curve of his waist and the strong of his back, but from the jagged piercings he’d done and the wonky braid of his hair. He’d recognize the marks of the life they’ve built, the history of what they now have.

And so even before they turn around, in a sea of people he doesn’t know, he can already tell that this is not Mydei.

Similar nose but brown eyes, the same shade of blonde hair but missing the braid and kept much longer without the red tips, the same cut of jaw and brows, but without the slight crook of his nose and tattoos on his skin.

But maybe most obvious of all, was that the person standing in front of him is no man at all. It was a middle aged woman, staring very funnily at him.

“Hello? Did you need anything?”

The roar of the crowd is deafening, loud and overbearing all at once after he finally snaps back and refocuses on what he’s doing. Phainon blinks once, then twice, and before his brain shuts down from embarrassment he remembers that he is An Adult and should thus be respectful to his elders.

“Oh! Hi!” He blinks innocently, like he hadn’t just stopped a random woman at a crowded convention after hallucinating that she was his roommate. “Sorry ma’am, I’d just meant to warn you that your shoelaces were untied!”

She blinks, then looks down on her flats, sleek and black and decidedly without shoelaces, and stifles a laugh. “Right. Of course. Are you concussed?”

“What makes you say that?”

He wishes the earth would swallow him up whole.

“Oh, nevermind me,” she waves him off, “But that’s okay, I need some help. Are you familiar with this place, dear? I’ve been trying to find the museum but I’ve been walking in circles. That directory hasn’t been much help, either.” She points at the map of the convention, jutting her thumb out.

Phainon looks over at the map. The museum itself was split into two– a convention center and the museum with a conjoined common area for headlining events. She must have gotten lost in the convention center, he realizes, maybe she was heading to the exhibitions area.

“Did you mean to head here?” He pulls out his phone, scrolling through a few images of the area, “That’s the permanent exhibitions center, on the other wing of the complex. This here is for exhibitions.”

The woman squints, before nodding to herself. “That sounds right, yes,” she mumbles, taking out her own phone, “do you mind if I take a picture?”

Phainon has more decency than to judge technical inabilities, but sometimes he gets truly close to crossing his own morals. Even seeing someone bad with technology is making me miss Mydei. Damn . Withdrawals were hitting hard.

It wasn’t even the first time it’s happened. The last time Mydei worked overtime at the library after they’d received a new shipment of books, Phainon had to stop himself after spending five whole minutes on the sidewalk talking to an orange cat.

He’d only truly realized he'd been talking to an animal after the cat had scratched him once he’d finished his long-winded rant about why red was the obvious compliment to purple. Now, everytime he walks past it, the same cat with a scar under its eye and the most judgemental yellow eyes known to man, Phainon (scornfully) nods his head in acknowledgement. Its name from then on was Meow-dei.

“If you don’t mind, I could instead walk you to the other wing? I wouldn’t want you to be lost,” he offers tentatively.

The woman hums contemplatively as she checks her phone and huffs. “That would be ideal. I’ll be meeting with my son soon you see, he’d wait for me for hours, here. I haven’t visited in a while.”

Her admittance is coupled with a smile, slow and fond as she looks at her phone. It’s an old thing, one camera, still with the chunky sides and her clear phone case yellowed, but there’s a polaroid in the back, stained from its age. He can’t see the picture from here, but he can tell it’s a cherished photo.

“He sounds lovely,” Phainon smiles as he pulls out his map, “the walk there isn’t too far, so we can meet up with him soon, how’s that?”

“Go on then,” she says, prompting him to walk.

They make it for about three minutes before she starts again. “Ah, but he really is quite lovely. Sweet boy, loves history. He got our tickets, months in advance, and planned the whole thing. Isn’t that cute?” She laughs, soft and bright.

Phainon’s heart warmed. It was clear just how much the two loved each other, an infectious pride in how she carried herself, not worn with her age but truly living it. She seemed content– radiant, even. She must really love her son.

“I’m sure he is. He’s picked a great spot. Okhema’s National Museum is excellent– I’ve been here a lot with my roommate. You see, I quite like history, too. This place is a gem for artifacts, they’ve got them from all over Amphoreus!”

“Do they now? I wouldn’t count myself a history buff, but I do love my tales. We better hurry up, better too early than late.”

Phainon was deliberately slowing his pace, he didn’t want to tire out the sweet middle-aged woman he’d just met, but in an instant she walked fast, fast enough to outpace him . Phainon looked in disbelief as he broke out into a jog to catch up to her.

As they walked, the crowd faded past as he kept track of the small of her back, and her shoulder length hair from behind, careful not to lose sight of her. She wasn’t nearly as tall as him, nor did she have the same presence in each of her steps, but there truly was something similar between her and Mydei. The same confidence in each step, the conviction for those that they loved.

Fuck. He’s really pushing it. That was a stretch, even for him.

Phainon shook his head, waving the thought away. What mattered now was ensuring the sweet lady he just met doesn’t get lost in the sea of convention goers, and gets to the more peaceful museum side safely. What matters even more though is being able to catch up, because even in flats and a long skirt, the woman manages to outpace him effortlessly.

When they finally make it past the booths and displays, the woman finally stops, waiting for him to catch up.

She laughs, almost to herself, “Trouble keeping up?” She says playfully.

“Hardly,” Phainon laughs, though slightly out of breath, “Sorry I lagged behind, it seems you’re much faster than I, ma’am.”

“Oh stop it, a young man like yourself should have no trouble keeping pace. My son did the same as a child. And stop with calling me ma’am, boy, and stop apologizing. You remind me of my lawyers.”

Phainon chuckled, rubbing the back of his neck sheepishly. “Habit! Sor-” he cuts himself off as the woman glares at him. He clears his throat, “Alright, what should I call you then, instead?”

The woman grins, like she’s been expecting this.

“Why don’t you hazard a guess, Phainon?”

Mydei doesn’t often talk about his family, though Phainon’s been able to piece together why.

His mother moved with him to Okhema, but these days she often lives in Castrum Kremnos a few hours away. His mother works with artifacts, and preserving their local culture, and is also, apparently, a better fighter than Mydei is.

Mydei’s love of jewelry is from his mother, who has a collection of all their family’s heirlooms. Her necklaces, rings and bracelets, the only things she’d gotten out of the divorce, along with custody of Mydei himself. He speaks of her fondly, his habits of cooking and gifting are remnants of how fiercely he’s always been loved.

Once, on Phainon’s 21st birthday, just around the time they’d moved in together, Mydei had introduced him to honeycakes and pomegranates.

Kremnoan culture was hard to come by in the Holy City. You’d see plenty of Janusapolian cuisine, Aidonian clothing and travel guides or even Styxian delicacies here and there, but little was known of Kremnos– only the persisting stereotype that Kremnoans were brutish, somewhat. Maybe that’s why Mydei himself was so protective of his culture.

Despite this, the moment they’d moved out and after the little get-together they’d held with college friends, Mydei was the one who proposed to celebrate with his region’s delicacies in the comfort of their new home. Handmade pomegranate juice, made with the fruits his mother had shipped straight to their apartment and the tallest stack of honeycakes he’s ever seen in his life.

Mydei had laughed vindictively as Phainon’s mouth soured, immediately trying to fix a shaky grin as he took a sip of the juice. “Wow- wow! Cough, that- that sure is something,” he said, wheezing.

It was sour, floral in the way it felt like someone had shoved you face down into a field of them, overbearingly sweet while also not quite being sweet enough. It had a distinctly alcoholic taste to it that he’s sure was more than just from the pomegranate. “What did you put into this?” He asks, groaning as he rests his head on their countertop in defeat. He really couldn’t take another sip. There’s no way that was just juice.

Mydei shoves him playfully eliciting protest as he finishes off the cup Phainon had drunk from, barely a reaction from him. “What a weak man you are, HKS. To think you’d be so easily defeated by juice.”

“That’s not fair,” he groans, “you must’ve spiked my drink!”

Mydei scoffs, “So now you accuse me of being dishonourable?”

“I’m accusing you of being a sadist, that’s what it is. What was in my cup? Don’t tell me it’s just juice, I don’t believe you. It was alcohol, wasn’t it? Whose? We don’t keep liquor around the house.”

“We’ve quite literally just moved in.”

“And I packed over half those boxes. No alcohol, I can assure it!”

Mydei hums, topping off a different glass with the juice, but now adding a heaping pour of milk and ice cream and topping it with a bright pink twisty straw. He takes a sip, before nodding, satisfied, and sliding it back over to Phainon, who drinks it with a satisfied smile on his face.

“You packed exactly half, Phainon. I counted, don’t get ahead of yourself. If you are concerned about alcohol around the house, I had received some, from my mother, she’d sent it along with the pomegranates.”

“Aha!” Phainon exclaims, snapping his fingers as he gets up triumphantly, “So there was alcohol!
